title: Makita XSH06PT 18V X2 LXT® Lithium-Ion (36V) Brushless Cordless 7-1/4” Circular Saw Kit (5.0Ah)

reviews.title: Really great saw to replace my Makita XSS02Z
reviews.body: The 6.5" BRUSHED Makita XSS02Z was my first tool as a homeowner ~11 years ago. It served me well for light duty, but as the years went on and my DIY projects increased in scope, the little old saw just couldn't keep up. It would chug, over heat, burn your hands even.Enter XSH06Z (via the XSH06PT kit I ordered here) - this thing is a BEAST. Heavier by a noticeable amount, yes. But it cuts through boards like they are nothing. The blade sits on the right side compared to my old Makita which was on the left. Not sure I care too much, just have to get used to it. The marks and guides make so much more sense on this one. The blade stop and blade retention screw are intuitive. It's significantly quieter and has that brushless ramp up/down. A small complaints though: The batteries arrived completely dead, zero juice, which isn't good for most batteries. The blade depth markings are a little hard to read in an awkward gap between the handle and guard. The safety switch is a small button and less of a lever that I liked on the smaller model.Other than that, these dual battery chargers are great. My last one started dying after ~5 years so it was perfect to pick up this dual kit. The OEM Makita batteries are also hard to find a good deal on, but in a kit these 5 amp are a pretty good deal. The tote bag as always is kind of useless.

reviews.body: This thing cuts tough boards like butter! It's a little bit heavier than some other saws due to the dual batteries, but that's what sets it apart. The 36v dual battery system really gives this saw a lot of power. It makes my 120V saw look weak! I love it and would highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Excellent and Convenient; Wish It Had a Hard-shell Case Rather Than a Bag
reviews.body: This is one of those "why didn't I do it sooner" products.  My 20-year old corded saw was inconvenient and dangerous.  My son "demanded" that I get rid of it. He was correct.  I did.  A friend told me he had switched to the Makita 18v system for all of his new power tools.  After checking out several reviews I took the plunge and glad I did.  I've since added the Makita 18v leaf blower and string trimmer to my tool shed.  I ordered the "kit" (with batteries) for the saw and just the "Tool Only" for the others.  For my limited use, 2 batteries are sufficient.  If you plan to use any of the items for big projects or long periods, order 2 extra batteries (shop around...I'm told the generics work as well and are half the price.)The only thing I dislike is that it comes in a soft-sided bag rather than a hard-sided case.  Yes, the bag gives extra room and allows for more things to be carried, but I prefer a hard-case for a number of reasons.  1. It keeps the tool in place and safe from damage.  2. It allows the tool box to be stacked on a shelf, out of the way, for storage.  I've looked for a hard-shell case for this saw but can't find one. (If anyone knows of one, please reply and post the information.)

reviews.author: Lee Bonney

reviews.title: Excellent cordless saw
reviews.body: This is a great cordless option for the job site. I have worked in construction for about 30 years. This saw is strong enough to crosscut and plunge cut pressure treated lumber no problem. The saw comes with a framing blade that has a very thin kerf. The battery life is very good. I use the Makita 18v LXT line so I always have plenty of batteries anyway, but four 5ah batteries and a charger will last all day. The saw is probably a little on the heavy side for some, but if you are use to construction work then you won’t have any issue with the weight. To me it weighs about the same as a circular saw with a cord. Not having to deal with the cord all day is worth the weight. I had concerns before buying the saw because of a video review on you tube. In the video it shows a problem with the blade guard hanging up. I didn’t have a problem with this issue. The guard pushes back smooth when making cuts. The one in the review more than likely was a defect. I have over a dozen Makita 18v LXT tools. Two of them are over 10 years old. I only had a problem with a defective tool once. Good news is Makita has a great warranty.

features: Powered by two LXT batteries; x2 LXT technology delivers more power, speed and run time without the hassles of a cord
Makita built electronically controlled BL motor delivers 6, 000 RPM for maximum performance and 50% longer run time per charge
The BL Brushless motor eliminates carbon brushes, enabling the BL motor to run cooler and more efficiently for longer life
Automatic speed change technology adjusts cutting speed and torque during cut for optimum performance
X2 LXT technology delivers up to 610 crosscuts per charge in 2x4 spf lumber and up to 320 crosscuts per charge in 2x10 spf lumber using two 5.0Ah batteries
